title: √2 — Pythagoras' Constant
subtitle: Algebraic irrational · Geometry
summary: Diagonal of the unit square. First proved irrational.
detail:
\[ \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41421356237309\ldots \]

The irrationality of \(\sqrt{2}\) was proved by the Pythagoreans (a landmark in mathematics history) by showing that any ratio \(p/q\) in lowest terms would require both \(p\) and \(q\) to be even — a contradiction. The best rational approximations come from the convergents of its continued fraction \([1;2,2,2,\ldots]\): \(1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29,\ldots\)
